title: structured output: constrained decoding backends — CFG/regex/tokenizer edgecases & stability fixes
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve the constrained decoding subsystem used for structured output generation (CFG/grammar + regex constraints) and harden interactions with the tokenizer. Users reported malformed outputs under certain tokenizer boundary conditions and rare crashes when using regex backends with unicode/emoji-heavy inputs. This PR unifies the backend abstractions, adds tokenizer-aware constraint compilation, and includes fallback/error modes to preserve streaming stability and OpenAI-compat function/tool-calling behavior.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced a ConstrainedBackend interface to standardize CFG and regex implementations and make switching/combining backends deterministic.
- Tokenizer-aware constraint compiler: constraints are compiled against token sequences (prefix/suffix-aware) rather than raw bytes to avoid mismatches caused by byte-level regexes and multibyte UTF-8 characters.
- Regex backend: added unicode normalization (+NFKC option), grapheme cluster-aware anchors, and an optimized DFA fallback for long-run regexes to avoid recursion/stack issues.
- CFG backend: added lookahead-limited expansion controls and streaming-friendly pruning to keep memory bounded for high-throughput streaming.
- Tokenizer edgecases: fixes for subword-prefix tokens (e.g., leading spaces in English BPE; language-specific prefix tokens), handling of zero-width joiners, and normalization differences between the OpenAI-compatible tokenizer and our internal runtime tokenizer.
- API compatibility: ensured constrained decoding still works with the OpenAI compatibility layer (function/tool calling + structured outputs) by adding a compatibility shim that maps OpenAI-style constraints into our backend interface.
- Tests: added unit, fuzz, and integration tests covering emoji/unicode, long sequences, and combined CFG+regex constraints; added a reproducible test case from a customer incident.
- Docs: updated structured-output docs with notes on tokenizer caveats and recommended fallbacks (best-effort, strict, permissive modes).

Why this approach: Tokenization mismatches were the root cause of many malformed outputs when constraints were expressed over characters/regexes intended for raw text. Compiling constraints to operate on token sequences avoids mismatches and enables efficient streaming checks. Standardizing the backend interface makes future backends (e.g., neural constraint scorers) pluggable.

Backward compatibility and migration: Default behavior is unchanged for existing customers. The new tokenizer-aware compilation is enabled by default for all OpenAI-compat routes and can be disabled via a flag for experimental use. Existing saved constraint artifacts remain supported; a best-effort recompile is attempted on load and logged if there are deviations.

Performance: Microbenchmarks show a median decoding overhead of +3% for typical CFG-only workloads and up to +12% for pathological regex workloads, but worst-case latency spiking is mitigated by the DFA fallback and streaming pruning. We added a warning metric for "constrained_decoding_slow_path" to alert on high CPU/policy fallback rates.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests: 58 new unit tests for tokenizer interactions and backend behavior.
- Fuzz tests: harness added to perf-canary to run corpus from incident; reproduces previously observed crash.
- Integration: synthetic load test with streaming enabled and function-calling flows through OpenAI-compat layer.
- Manual: reproduced the customer incident and validated the fixed behavior end-to-end.

Rollout plan: Merge to main, monitor new metric for 72h, enable conservative fallback mode by default for Hosted API for one week, and then progressively enable stricter compilation after validation.

Checklist:

- [x] Doc updates
- [x] Perf benchmarks run
- [x] Reviewed by runtime and dx teams

References: ENG-4321 (structured-output hardening), ENG-4987 (tokenizer mismatch incident), internal incident report: INC-2026-01-14.
